t: many characters. Different character traits and dispositions.
and this one is different from that, and extremely far from it. There may be extreme differences between people's dispositions, as illustrated below.
once in several years. Once in a few years, rarely.
haughty. Proud.
lowly of spirit. Humble.
pure of body. Free of bodily desire.
a broad soul. Pursuing wealth.
narrow. Who has no desire at all for possessions.
afflicts himself with hunger and gathers by hand etc.. Fasts from hunger out of extreme stinginess and thrift.
destroys all his money by his own hand knowingly. Squanders his money intentionally.
raving and mourning. Constantly raving or grieving.
miser and generous. Stingy or generous toward others.
intermediate dispositions. Middle ones.
this one is far from that one. For there are many possibilities for intermediate traits.

and conducts himself by it until it becomes fixed. There are traits to which a person has no innate inclination or natural talent to attain, but which are acquired through a person's consistent conduct according to his decision.
and this is the straight path. This is what the middle path is called.
for it is equally distant from the two extremes. That is, exactly in the middle.
he sets his dispositions. He estimates and measures them.
so that he will be whole. Perfected in his character traits.
a hot-tempered person, quick to anger. Gets angry easily.
like a dead person who does not feel. Who does not respond at all to things done against his will.
but only over a great matter etc.. Only if the anger is justified and has benefit for the future (and see below 2:3).
without them. Without them.
the righteous eats to satisfy his soul. To fulfill the needs of the soul's life.
to obtain something he needs for the needs of the moment. What he needs for his sustenance, and not in order to become wealthy.
and he should not close his hand. He should not close his hand from giving his money.
according to what his hand can afford. According to his ability.
to one who needs. To one who needs money.
a little toward this side or that side. Toward one of the sides that has some advantage.
and the early pious ones would incline their dispositions from the middle path etc.. They would act so, in a small way, in each trait, as a fence for their conduct (see Shemoneh Perakim, chapter 4).
beyond the line of the law. Beyond what is required by law.
"and you shall walk in His ways". In the ways of God.
to make known that these are good and straight ways etc.. The prophets chose these appellations because they characterize proper conduct.
until they become fixed in him. Until he becomes accustomed to those good traits, so that they become part of his nature.
he should do it and repeat it and do it a third time. He should repeat a second and third time.
for these names by which the Creator is called. "Slow to anger and abundant in kindness" and all the epithets mentioned above in 1:6.

the sick of body etc.. There are people sick with physical illnesses that disrupt the sense of taste, so that sometimes they will want to eat things that a healthy person finds no pleasure in, and which are even harmful to the body.
according to the severity of the illness. According to the seriousness of the disease.
whose souls are sick. Accustomed to flawed character traits.
and it is very heavy upon them. Difficult for them to carry out.
Woe to those who call evil good. Woe to those who err and think that evil is good.
who abandon paths of uprightness to walk in ways of darkness. They do not walk in a good and upright path, and prefer over it an evil and dark path.
and fools despise instruction. Fools scorn words of moral instruction and rebuke, and are not interested in improving their conduct by them.
a hot-tempered person. An angry person.
should not feel at all. Should not respond to those things.
until anger is uprooted from his heart. Until anger ceases to arise in him each time something happens that is not to his liking.
haughty. Proud.
and return to the middle path, which is the good path. After uprooting the extreme trait from himself, he will be able to walk the middle way.
and along this line. In this manner and way.
and those who love Him are like the sun going forth in its might. Although they are now lowly, in the future they will shine like the sun at its strength.
for it is forbidden for a person to follow the middle course in them. Because even in the middle measure of these there is a flaw and defect.
for the good path is not merely that a person be humble. That is the middle trait, but there is great praise in extreme lowliness.
for anyone who becomes haughty has denied the fundamental principle. Because he treats his own personality as idolatry.
excommunicated be he who has arrogance. Let one who has arrogance be under a ban.
and it is fitting for a person to distance himself from it to the other extreme. That he become accustomed to not being angry at all.
even over something about which it is proper to be angry. And this is distancing from anger to the other extreme (and above 1:4 the middle measure of this trait was explained).
to instill fear in his children and household. So that they will fear him and behave properly.
a leader. A community leader.
he should show himself to them as angry. He should pretend as if he is angry.
to discipline them. To reprove them.

anyone who gets angry is as if he worships idols. And they connected this to the verse "There shall be no strange god within you," for when he gets angry it is as if he lets a strange god take control of him.
and the angry have no life that is life. Because everything done against their wishes disturbs their peace.
insulted but not insulting. Others insult them, but they do not insult others.
in a matter of wisdom. Words of thought or Torah, as below.
Rav. The head of the Babylonian Amoraim in the first generation of Amoraim, and a student of Rabbi Yehudah ha-Nasi, the editor of the Mishnah ("Rabbenu ha-Kadosh").
and this is the speech of most people. Idle talk.
and even about bodily needs a person should not speak much. Even though it is permitted to talk about them.
anyone who multiplies words brings sin. For if he talks too much, he will come to say what should not be said.
the words of a wise man are few and their content is great. He will be brief in his speech and include many subjects in it.
a short way. In concise and precise wording.
if the words are many and the matter little, this is folly. If the subject is short and the words about it are many, this is foolishness.
for a dream comes with much business. Vain words are said in great detail.
and a fool's voice with many words. Foolish words are said in a multitude of words.
silence is a fence for wisdom. Silence helps to preserve wisdom.
he should not hasten to answer. Rather, he should wait in silence.
calmly and quietly. With calm and ease.
without lengthiness of speech. Briefly.
with smooth words and enticement. Words of flattery and falsehood.
his inside is like his outside. His inner self is the same as his outer self.
to steal the minds of people. To deceive them.
even the mind of a gentile. It is forbidden to deceive (just as in monetary law it is forbidden to rob or deceive him - Hilchot Genevah 7:8, Hilchot Gezelah va-Avedah 11:3-5).
the meat of a nevelah included with slaughtered meat etc.. Because he thinks he is giving him higher-quality, more expensive meat.
a shoe of a dead animal. Made from the hide of an animal that died, whose value is less than that of a slaughtered animal.
he should urge. He should press.
and he knows that he will not eat etc.. And in all these deceptions he causes his friend to think that he intends to honor him.
with gifts. With presents.
words of truth. Truthful speech.
and a steadfast spirit and a heart pure of all toil and vanity. Intentions clean of falsehood and evil.
but cheerful. This is the middle trait.
they lead to sexual immorality. They may lead to the sin of forbidden relations.
with a pleasant countenance. With pleasantness.
hastening to wealth. Chasing money (based on Proverbs 28:22).
a little business and engaged in Torah. A person who minimizes business and does only as much as he needs for his livelihood (see above 1:4, Hilchot Talmud Torah 3:7-9).
envy, lust, and honor remove a person from the world. For they are traits that harm the person himself.
and all your ways will be established. They will all be firm, being directed by the middle path.
since lust, honor, and the like are an evil path. As above 2:7.
to the other extreme. To the opposite extreme.
until he does not eat meat etc.. All these are among bodily desires.
but sackcloth and coarse wool. He wears them so as not to enjoy his clothing.
such as the priests of Edom. For Christian priests and monks conduct themselves in such ascetic matters.
and make atonement for him for having sinned regarding the soul. Said of one who vowed to be a nazir and became impure during his nazirite period.
who abstained only from wine. For a nazir is forbidden everything that comes from the vine (see Hilchot Nezirut 1:1).
needs atonement. For having forbidden himself enjoyment of something.
one who denies himself everything. Abstains from all enjoyment.
except from things that the Torah alone prohibited. Only things forbidden according to halachah.
and this is included in this etc.. These too are included in the Sages' command not to forbid what is permitted.
why should you be desolate. Excessive asceticism brings ruin and harm.
that he direct all his deeds to know the Blessed Name alone. That all his actions in bodily matters be for this purpose.
for this matter. For this intention.
that he find things the body needs. That he can supply his bodily needs with this money.
he should not set his mind to do these things merely to enjoy. These actions should not be done solely for pleasure.
he should eat things that benefit him. Foods that are good for the body's health (for details see below, chapter 4).
one whose flesh is hot etc.. For according to medicine these foods harm his body.
and drinks endive water. Water in which endive was steeped, which is beneficial for healing.
so that he eats and drinks only by way of medicine. His eating and drinking are not for enjoyment but to sustain the body and heal it.
to make his body healthy. That there is a health need for this (for details see below 4:19).
and to preserve the seed. To have children.
this is not a good path. For he sees only the good of his body.
to know the Lord. To contemplate the existence of the Creator and His unity, which are positive commandments (see Hilchot Yesodei ha-Torah 1:1-7).
and he should set his mind to have a son etc.. That this be his purpose in having children.
he serves the Lord always. In all his deeds, all of which are for the purpose of serving God.
that his mind be at ease with it. That his thought be calm.
"in all your ways know Him". That all your actions be for the sake of knowing God.
since a healthy and whole body is among the ways of the Lord etc.. See above 3:3.
from things that destroy the body. That cause the body harm.
those that heal and restore health. That bring health and recovery.
and he should not delay his orifices. He should not hold back from relieving himself if needed (see also Hilchot Ma'achalot Asurot 17:31).
he should eat about a quarter less than his satiety. He should eat a quarter less than he needs to be full.
in the middle of the meal. In the midst of the meal.
until he examines himself very well. He should make sure he does not need to relieve himself.
to be warm. To warm up.
let him exert himself with another exertion. That exercises and warms the body.
and be quiet. Rest.
or recline on his left. This is eating in the manner of reclining (see Hilchot Berakhot 7:1, Hilchot Chametz u-Matzah 7:7-8).
and they should be at the end of the night. Those same eight hours in which he sleeps.
not on his face and not on his back but on his side. See Hilchot Keriat Shema 2:2, Hilchot Issurei Bi'ah 21:19.
right after eating. Immediately after eating.
and the insides of cucumbers. Their inner part, which contains the seeds.
and he should not mix them with the meal etc.. So that they do not mix even during digestion.
from the upper belly. From the stomach.
they strengthen the intestines. They harden the intestines so that they tend toward constipation.
and quinces. Quinces.
and wild pears. Wild pears.
immediately after his meal. Immediately after eating the food.
he first eats poultry. Which is easier to digest than meat of animals.
and he should not use many spices. For spices heat the body.
of mustard and asafoetida. Which are sharp and heat the body.
such as large, salted, old fish etc.. Old things that salt preserves from spoiling.
and wine straight from the press. Which was pressed and has not yet fermented.
and a cooked dish that sat until its smell faded. That time passed over it until it began to spoil.
deadly poison. Poison.
are not as bad as the first ones. They harm less than the foods listed above.
a little and after many days. In small quantity and rarely.
and the sapir. Peas.
and in the rainy season. Because digesting these foods strains the body and heats it (as above 4:8).
for they are bad but not like these. Eating them harms less.
and fine flour that was sifted as much as needed etc.. That was cleaned entirely of the husks of the wheat kernel.
and tzir. What comes from salted, pickled fish.
and muries. A sauce made from fish innards.
and needless to say, fresh ones. Which are even worse than dried ones.
are like swords to the body. And actually harmful.
but he should not eat them continually. He should not eat them always, but only occasionally.
bad for the young and good for the old. Harmful to the young and beneficial to the elderly.
and all the more so in the rainy season. When they benefit the elderly, because they warm.
two thirds of what he eats in the rainy season. So that in summer the body will exert itself less in the digestion process and not overheat.
loose. Loose.
for the stool is held back. The excrement is held back.
if he was a young man. A young person.
salty plants. Leaves of the saltwort plant (a desert plant with broad, salty leaves).
an old man. An older person.
exercises and exerts himself much. Works his body and tires it (above 4:2).
sits securely. Without toil or movement.
who delays his orifices. Holds back (above 4:1).
grows weak. Weakens.
and gluttonous eating. Excessive, extreme eating.
and his tongue from speaking except for his needs. That a person should speak as little as he can (above 2:4).
from seven days to seven days. Once a week.
in hot water in which the body is scalded. Very hot water.
until he washes in cold water. He should gradually move to cold water.
and he should not wash in cold water in the rainy season. So that his body does not get too cold.
and his whole body is exhausted. He becomes tired from the bathing.
but when he sweats and his body is exhausted, he rinses and leaves. For at this stage bathing begins to be harmful.
and examines himself. Whether he needs to relieve himself.
and when he wakes. Gets up from his sleep.
all together ten. In total ten checks.
in the outer room. The outer room of the bathhouse in which one gets dressed (see Hilchot Tefillin 4:22).
to let blood. Drawing blood from the body as a medical procedure.
except in the days of Nisan and a little in the days of Tishrei. When the weather is pleasant.
and after fifty years. After the age of fifty.
and a person should not let blood etc.. One should not let blood when the body is weak, or will be weak after the bloodletting.
wearing out. Wearing away.
coming to an end. Finishing.
your strength. Your strength.
and your ways to destroy kings. Do not, through your conduct, cause the loss of your future as a king.
old age springs upon him. He ages quickly.
grows weak. Weakens.
increasing. Multiplying.
when he finds his body healthy and very strong. And not when it is weak.
not of his own will. Not voluntarily.
and distracts himself with something else. Tries to occupy himself with other things.
neither before them nor after them. For those are times of bodily weakness.
I guarantee him. He is assured.
his body was bad from the beginning of his creation. That it had inborn defects.
and a change of routine is the beginning of illness. Changing habits causes diseases.
it is not fitting for him to deviate from any of these ways. In the absence of another recommendation, one should act according to what is stated here.
a Torah scholar may not dwell in it. Because those things are necessary for an orderly life, and a Torah scholar should be careful about this.
and a craftsman. One who lets blood.
and a teacher of children. Who teaches them Torah (see also Hilchot Talmud Torah 2:1).
and a scribe. One engaged in the work of writing.
and a court that strikes and imprisons. Authorities empowered to flog and imprison offenders.
and he is distinguished by them from the rest of the people. He is recognizable from them as a person of stature, different and special.
and in the management of his affairs. The conduct of his financial matters (see below 5:10).
glutton. Gorger.
to be healthy. To become healthy.
gluttonous eating. Excessive, extreme eating.
that their bellies swell. That their stomachs be bloated.
"and I will spread dung upon your faces, the dung of your festivals". I will throw in your faces the excrement produced by overeating.
and they make all their days like festivals. On which they indulge in feasting and rejoicing (see Hilchot Yom Tov 6:17-18).
and they are the ones who say, "Eat and drink, for tomorrow we die". Those people who eat excessively do so because they pursue pleasures as long as they can engage in them.
for all tables are full of filthy vomit, with no place left. Such a meal is likened to filth, which ends up that way and serves no other purpose.
but one dish or two. He is not eager to glorify his meal, but is satisfied with what is necessary.
for his life. As much as is needed for his bodily life (see above 3:2, 4:2).
he should not eat in a shop or in the marketplace. See Hilchot Edut 11:5.
and not at those tables etc.. Together with people eager for the pleasure of eating (above 5:1).
provided that he is a Torah scholar who married the daughter of a Torah scholar. This is a fitting and proper match (see Hilchot Issurei Bi'ah 21:32).
never ate from a meal that was not their own. They did not want to benefit from property not their own (and see Hilchot Zekhiyah u-Matanah 12:17).
only to soak the food in his intestines. So that the food will digest well.
he has desecrated the Name. See Hilchot Yesodei ha-Torah 5:11.
and it is forbidden to drink at noon. For if he becomes drunk at noon he will lose the rest of the day.
and one need beware only of wine after the meal. Which is intoxicating.
like a rooster. One who engages excessively in marital relations (see Hilchot Issurei Bi'ah 21:11).
from Friday night to Friday night. Which is the time for Torah scholars (Hilchot Ishut 14:1).
if he has the strength. If he is healthy and able to (see Hilchot Ishut 14:7).
converses with her. Has marital relations with her.
not at the beginning of the night etc.. See above 4:19, Hilchot Ishut 21:10.
nonsense. Vanity.
and not sluggish. Tired.
and he should not force her. He should not compel her (see Hilchot Issurei Bi'ah 21:12).
for if he had children. If children were born to him from this relationship.
they have handsome and bashful children etc.. They merit good qualities because their creation was in holiness.
he has children like those people. Without special qualities.
and they should not uncover their head or their body. They should not expose them, out of modesty.

and he should not wipe with his right hand. He should not wipe himself in the restroom with the right hand, which is the honored hand (see, for example, Hilchot Tefillah 14:3, Hilchot Bi'at ha-Mikdash 5:18).
a room within a room, inside the cave. Where there is additional concealment.
and if he relieves himself behind a fence. And not in a restroom.
sneezes. Emits a sound while relieving himself.
in a valley. An open field, where nothing conceals him.
his exposure. Uncovering the body.

to relieve himself morning and evening etc.. In the morning and evening when many people are not out, because if he relieves himself in the middle of the day he will need to go a great distance for the sake of modesty (see also Hilchot Ma'achalot Asurot 17:31).
his speech gently. Calmly (see also Hilchot Yesodei ha-Torah 5:11).
he should be careful not to distance himself. He should not slow his speech too much.
and he greets everyone first. He addresses them with a greeting of peace.
and if not, he is silent. And refrains from saying something that will not be accepted.
he should appease. He should placate.
he should ask about his vow. To annul the vow if he regrets it (for the method of annulment see Hilchot Shevuot, chapter 6).
until his mind cools and settles. He calms from the turbulence of spirit because of which he vowed.
because he is agitated until he is buried. For his mind is not settled at this time (see also Hilchot Evel 4:6).
and he should not appear to his fellow etc.. He should try not to appear before him when he is doing something improper, so as not to embarrass him.
and he should not alter his speech. To say something untrue.
except in words of peace and the like. For it is permitted to deviate from the truth to bring peace between a person and his fellow (see also Hilchot Gezelah va-Avedah 14:13).
even if she is his wife or his sister or his daughter. Since not everyone knows they are relatives, and it looks improper.
outstretched. Extended.
as it says. In the prophet's words of rebuke toward the haughty daughters of Zion.
and winking with their eyes. Hinting with their eyes.
heel to toe, gently. Walking slowly in small steps.
and behave like a madman. For running in the public domain is unusual behavior (see Hilchot Chovel u-Mazik 6:9).
like those with a hunchback. Like a hunchback.
he looks downward like one standing in prayer. For during the Amidah prayer one must direct his eyes downward, as if looking at the ground (see Hilchot Tefillah 5:4).
at an even pace. At the proper speed.
his heart is lacking. He lacks sense.
and he tells everyone he is a fool. From his conduct everyone understands that he is a fool.
and it is forbidden for him to be found with a stain on his garment etc.. For this is a disgrace.
for everyone looks at them. They are exceptional in importance.
middle. Average.
his undergarment. His shirt.
the finest. Very thin.
dragging on the ground. Long garments that trail on the ground.
to his heels. A shirt that covers the whole leg.
and his sleeve to the tips of his fingers. The sleeve covers the hand (see Hilchot Kelei ha-Mikdash 8:17).
and he should not let his cloak hang down. He should not spread it out unfolded, for this is a manner of honor and greatness (see Hilchot Kelei ha-Mikdash 8:4).
except on Shabbat only etc.. Out of respect for Shabbat (see also Hilchot Shabbat 30:3).
patched in the garment. With pieces of cloth.
but in the rainy season it is permitted. For then there is no choice.
perfumed. Applied various perfumes to his body (see also Hilchot Berakhot 7:14).
because of suspicion. That he will be suspected of perfuming himself or of going out at night for immoral purposes.
manages his affairs with justice. Conducts his financial matters in a measured way.
according to his wealth and success etc.. According to his financial situation, and he should not become accustomed to things beyond his means.
but for desire. When he craves meat.
from Friday to Friday. Once a week.
the way of people of sound judgment. Who act according to logical order.

as it says, "And who is the man" etc.. In the Torah's commandments regarding going out to war, it says that the kohen speaks to the people and calls on anyone who planted a vineyard, built a house, or betrothed a woman to return home from the battle (see Hilchot Melakhim, chapter 7). And from this they infer that marrying a wife is mentioned last among these deeds.
he should go around seeking a trade or support himself from charity. He should look for a profession for himself, and if he does not find one, he should support himself from charity.
may your deeds be reversed. The curse is that you not conduct yourself the right way, and thereby a bad future will grow.
and he will trouble people. For if he has nothing, he will be forced to live off others (see also Hilchot Arachin ve-Charamin 8:13).
and he should not sell a field and buy a house. Since the profit of a field is greater.
is meticulous with himself in accounting. To pay everything he owes.
and he pays the purchase price immediately. If he has the ability to (Hilchot Yesodei ha-Torah 5:11).
immediately. At once.
neither a guarantor nor an undertaker. Those who take upon themselves to pay another person's debt, and may lose through no fault of their own (see Hilchot Malveh ve-Loveh 25:5).
and he should not come with a power of attorney. He should not be appointed as an agent to collect money from others (see Hilchot Sheluchin ve-Shutafin 3:5).

in a place where the Torah did not obligate him etc.. Even when by Torah law he is not obligated in something, he behaves as if he were obligated. For example, if he said that he would buy something, even though this is not a binding acquisition, he does not retract (Hilchot Mekhirah 7:8).
is patient with them. Does not get angry.
and lends and is gracious. Lends to them in time of need and has compassion on them.
and he should not go down into his fellow's craft. He should not engage in another's trade and compete with him.
distress. Trouble.
of the insulted and not of the insulters. See also Hilchot Talmud Torah 7:13.
"Israel, in whom I will be glorified". That God is glorified through him, and this is sanctification of the Name (Hilchot Yesodei ha-Torah 5:11).
the nature of a person's makeup. His habit by nature.
he who walks with the wise becomes wise, and a companion of fools will suffer. One who joins the wise becomes wise, whereas a friend of fools will be harmed by associating with them.
he should go to a place whose people are righteous. And not live in the neighborhood of wicked people (see also Hilchot Ishut 13:15).
because of the bands. For there is danger in traveling on the roads.
he should sit alone, solitary. He should keep away from the people of the country and not learn from their deeds.
and to the caves. To fortresses, protected places.

"Who will give me in the wilderness a lodging place of wayfarers". Would that I were in the wilderness, a place where travelers lodge (those on the road), and not in settled places where wicked people live.
to cleave to the wise. To be bound and close to them.
commerce. Trade.
covers himself in the dust of their feet etc.. Sits on the ground before them to hear their words.
and to have pity on his money. To be careful that his property not be damaged.
and one who glorifies himself through his fellow's disgrace. Builds his own honor on the degradation of another.
like his own body. As a person treats himself.
the convert who came and entered under the wings of the Shechinah. Who accepted the commandments and became Jewish (see Hilchot Issurei Bi'ah 13:4).
included among neighbors. Included in the category of "your neighbor," like any Jew.
in his heart. Without the hatred being expressed in action.
and one is not flogged for this prohibition, because it involves no action. For one is not flogged for a transgression unless it involves an actual action (Hilchot Sanhedrin 18:1-2).
one who strikes... and one who curses... although he is not permitted. For this is forbidden (below 5:8, Hilchot Chovel 5:1).
he should not hate him and remain silent. He should not hate him in his heart without saying anything to him.
"You shall surely rebuke your fellow". And the beginning of the verse: "You shall not hate your brother in your heart." That you not continue to carry in your heart the sin he committed against you.
and Abraham prayed to God. He prayed for the healing of Abimelech, king of the Philistines, and forgave him for taking Sarah his wife, after Abimelech asked for forgiveness.
it is a mitzvah to return him to the good path. To cause him to leave the sin (and see Hilchot Teshuvah 4:1).
for he sins against himself. He causes himself harm through his sins (see there 5:2).
between him and himself. Without others present.
"I do not listen". I do not listen to you or accept from you.
he should not speak harshly to him until he shames him. Until the friend is embarrassed by his words.
and you will not bear sin because of him. That you not sin in the words of rebuke.
and his face changes. His face turns pale from distress and shame.
so the Sages said: one who shames his fellow in public etc.. See Hilchot Teshuvah 3:14.
as he is ashamed of it. By the epithet that shames him.
if he did not retract in private. After having been rebuked discreetly.
and insult. Disgrace.
as all the prophets in Israel did. They did not refrain from rebuking them in public and in harsh language.
very ignorant. Quite lacking in wisdom, and does not understand the significance of his actions.
the Torah was concerned only about hatred. The main thing is that a person not hate his fellow, and in order that he not hate him, he must rebuke him.
to be careful with orphans and widows. Not to harm them (see Hilchot Yom Tov 6:18, Hilchot Megillah 2:17).
the widow of a king etc.. Who do not need financial help from people.
ruled over them. Made them do hard and painful work.
"He who said and the world came into being made a covenant with them". The Holy One, blessed be He, promised them.
cry out because of violence. They pray and complain about being oppressed.
but if the teacher afflicted them in order to teach them Torah or a trade etc.. For a teacher is permitted to strike students (see Hilchot Talmud Torah 2:2, Hilchot Rotzei'ach 5:6).
and nonetheless he should not treat them as he treats everyone. Even one who is permitted to cause them distress should not treat them as he treats others.
difference. Distinction.

until they no longer need a great person to rely on to raise them and take care of them. That they become grown enough and not need someone to raise them and care for them. [Note: Rambam in Perush ha-Mishnayot vocalizes the word "when" as "amatai."]
the talebearer. A gossiper, one who passes on information (below 5:2).
for one is not flogged for this prohibition. For it too is a prohibition without actual action (see above 6:5).
and causes the killing of many souls from Israel. May cause great harm, as below.
therefore it is juxtaposed to it. The end of that same verse.

what happened to Doeg the Edomite. Who told Saul that David had received help from Achimelech the kohen, and because of this a death sentence was decreed on all the kohanim of the city of Nov (I Samuel, chapter 22).
a bearer of matters. Loads things, like a peddler who carries merchandise from place to place.
he destroys the world. For this will arouse quarrels among people.
in his fellow's disgrace. Bad things the other did.
one who spreads a bad name about his fellow is called etc.. See Hilchot Na'arah Betulah 3:1.
but a master of evil speech. One who speaks evil that is not falsehood, unlike one who spreads a bad name.
about this the verse says, "May the Lord cut off all smooth lips". God punishes and destroys all who engage in forbidden speech.
and evil speech is equal to them all. As severe as these three sins (and see Hilchot Teshuvah 3:6).
denied the fundamental principle. The Master of the world.
evil speech kills three etc.. It causes harm to all parties involved in it.
and the one who accepts it more than the one who says it. His law is more severe, for had he not accepted it the harm would have been avoided.
the dust of evil speech. Speech that hints that there is something bad, without explicitly telling the matter (see Hilchot Issurei Bi'ah 22:19).
"Who will say to so-and-so" etc.. An expression of wonder at a person's conduct, or a hint at bad things.
blesses his neighbor in a loud voice etc.. For speaking of a person's good can be considered a curse.
in a manner of laughter and levity. As if he does not mean his words seriously.
like a madman who shoots firebrands, arrows, and death etc.. Like a person who plays the fool and does life-threatening things and claims that they were not done intentionally.
in a manner of deceit. As if he is not referring to that matter and that person.
"I do not know that these are the deeds of so-and-so" etc.. For I did not say anything explicitly.
whether one tells... in front of his fellow or not in his presence. There is no difference in the law whether the words are said in the presence of the person being discussed or not in his presence.
for they cause, if heard from person to person, harm to his fellow etc.. If they become publicized they may cause some harm.
the matter was already heard and known. The matter became public, and therefore from here on one who tells it does not cause harm.
provided that he does not intend to spread the word and reveal it further. That he not intend to publicize this rumor more widely.
that it is forbidden to live in their neighborhood. Lest he learn from their deeds (see above 6:1, Hilchot Tumat Tzara'at 16:10).
and the decree was sealed on our fathers in the wilderness only for evil speech. For the Israelites believed the words of the spies, who spoke ill of the land of Canaan (Numbers, chapters 13-14).
and although he is not flogged. Because there is no action (as above 7:1).
to pass over all the words of the world. That he forgive everything in this world.
for all, to those who understand, is vanity and nonsense etc.. Those who understand know that these matters have no value and do not justify a conduct of vengeance.
your axe. A tool used for digging and cutting.
and so David said in his good dispositions. In the prayer in which he asks God to save him in the merit of his good traits, he mentions that he does not repay evil to those who did him evil.
one who bears a grudge. Who preserves the memory of the offense.
"and I am not like you and I will not repay you according to your deeds". I do not act like you with a stingy eye, and I will not treat you as you treated me.
he should erase the matter from his heart. Erase the matter and not retain it.
lest he come to take revenge. Which is a more serious act, "which is an extremely bad disposition" (above 7:7).
and this is the proper disposition, by which settlement of the world can be sustained etc.. This is the proper conduct, which enables an orderly life in the world.
